ipc-title__text: The best Batman movie by far
ipc-html-content-inner-div: This movie will blow you away in many ways. The story is the typical "Good Vs Bad" that we have seen in countless movies before but the way the story is told is both unexpected and brilliant. It's a fairly long movie but the length never seems to be a problem because something is more or less happening all the time and the story progress all the time, so when the movie ends you don't feel like you have been sitting for almost two and a half hour, you just sit there with a huge "WoW" on your face.Heath Ledger as The Joker sets such a perfect example of excellent acting that I will not be surprised if hes performance will stand as a pure example of how a bad guy should be acted. He's calculated, deliberate, to the point. In other words, as far from a cliché that you can come. My hat off for hes performance, rest in peace Ledger, know that you have sett the perfect example of how things are meant to be done.The other actors are doing a very good job, from Bale to Oldman, everyone is doing their job splendid. And they have to do it, to be able to keep up with the acting Ledger is doing with the Joker. Bale has to be the perfect "Good guy" in order to take down the perfect "bad guy".All in all this is one of those movie you have to be insane to miss. If you're looking for a action movie that blow you away this is the one and only to see.

Gotham city is alive, it's a living, breathing utopia that build on such a massive scale it almost outdoes Heaths chilling interpretation of The Joker. Boy is this one haunting experience, not only is Heath unnaturally humours but at the same time he manages to chill you down to the bone and despite is 12 certificate I do not recommend this to anybody below the age of 15 simply due to the sheer nature of Heaths character. Not only is it the performance of his life but what a stunning final bow if you will to his career. 10 years on when people are asking about him, the Dark Knight will be the film they turn to.And while he might outshine the rest of this films outstanding cast he doesn't complete the film. Just like last time Bale seems suited to the role, as if he was born to play Bat Man. Maggie Gyllenhal, the superbly sexy and sophisticated Rachel doesn't pull any of that damsel in distress clique and last but by no means least the stunning transformation of Aaron Eckhart from Harvey Dent into the sadistic and saddening two face is Chilling to say the very least. But this is by no means a mere character film. The action seems unbeatably. When Batman soars from building to building so do the audience. When the Joker laughs his high pitch screech the audience cowers as if he were real. Are you scared yet?Horrific as it may be, The Dark Knight is by no means rough around the edges competently soaring from Amazing set piece to the other and at an impressive 152 minutes it's a mystery on how director Christopher Nolan managed to keep the pacing in such perfect condition. Could it be that in fact we are all so captivated by the macabre brought by Ledger. The strangeness amounting from his recent passing away. Or is it the action keeping us glued to the screen unable to blink for a mere second just in case you miss one of the plenty moments that quite literally take your breath away. The truth is that its all of these, glued together and pumped with steroids. If you only go see one film this year make sure it's this one. I wouldn't be half surprised if this were to win best picture at the academy. Boy I sure hope it does. In truth we all wish for our own personal Batman. If only to add a bit of mystery back into our society. If I were to fault it in any way I would start with its inability to juggle its mass amount of characters, In retrospect you could merely see this as a justified excuse for a repeated viewing. With a tension building, spine tingling score it seems The Dark Knight is near perfect.VERDICT: As near perfect as were ever going to get. Not only is The Dark Knight the greatest film of 2008 but it's also this decade's finest film. With its haunting performances and it's out of this world action this flies straight to the top of The Words film of the year list and nestles deep within our sole as the most powerful and disturbing superhero movie to date. The posters might say 12A but I wouldn't trust them. but be warned. The joker could stay in your nightmares for years.

Just one word for Heath Ledger, Oscar. And for those that don't understand... Best Supporting Actor. The perfect Villain 2nd only to the original Alien. I say no more. Heath was at his best in this movie. Too bad they spoiled Two Face. Batman has never meet a better villain. And It is a sad day when We can't enjoy a second go around with such a brilliant villain. No one can ply the part like he did again. And let's hope that the makers of the movie don't try to find a replacement. There is no way anyone can play the part to such a high level. Just like Jack in the first Batman, Heath stole the show, and then some. And yet I have to use ten lines to explain it. No way. Ten lines is a waste of time. Just one line will do. And the Oscar for Best Supporting Actor goes to... Heath Ledger.

For all the hype, the reviews and the posthumous Oscar nominations this film does not fail to entertain or provoke. As all have said The performance of Ledger is thoroughly enthralling, and is reminiscent in kind of Hopkins in Silence of the Lambs, that of a psychotic yet fascinating mind.However as a film it moves far beyond merely a great performance, it moves into the realm of modern day greats. The script, tone, score and cinematography of the film puts it in the class of epic. Unlike of comic book films of old, even crime films of old, it is not merely the protagonist taking on (a few) villains (e.g. Spiderman 3 where is was literally like taking down a series of video game bosses), but more an figure battling an idea. In the film it challenges what and who makes up the society we live in today, and the treatment hits home. It asks questions about whether our morality is forged by the society that governs us, or born out of an instrinsic sense of justice? Is it ever right to coerce the lives of individuals for the lives of many? Should people find the truth they want, or the truth they need? It even answers questions that writers such as Frank Miller brought up in their classic treatments of Batman and the Joker; are the Batman and the Joker merely hero and villain, or do they need each other for meaning to what they do? Beyond the philosophical wankery one always hears from film critics, the film is bloody awesome. The action sequences are so slick, stylish and gritty, the special effects are used in a way that they maintain their sense of scale and realism (take note Michael Bay) and the Joker is extremely funny.My 3 favourite films 3 weeks ago, were The Godfather, the Seventh Seal and Apocalypse now...

ipc-title__text: A challenge to its beginnings which falls short on greatness...
A saga of crime that is not expected of a superhero movie
ipc-html-content-inner-div: One week of release and The Dark Knight has broken every major box-office record it could, even touching IMDb's top spot in highest rated movies. This fervor, attributed mainly to the ingenious viral marketing campaign and the tragic demise of Heath Ledger, dictates the response to the movie being as emphatic as it is. Once the noise settles, sifting through that manic praise, the movie surfaces as a great crime-saga, even one of the best ever made. It just happens to be a Batman movie.In the closing moments of Batman Begins, we believe that Gotham city now has a savior in Batman. And quite so, The Dark Knight begins with batman-wannabes combating scared criminals, and nervous mob bosses holding meetings during the day. In the tradition of "Gravitas, Pietas, Dignitas" the new district attorney, Harvey Dent (Aaron Eckhart), joins forces with Lt. Gordon (Gary Oldman) and Batman (Christian Bale) to rinse Gotham of the crime wave that grips it. What they or the criminals don't expect is a madman, the Joker (Heath Ledger), taking matters into his own hands.Much like Batman, the Joker uses fear as his main weapon. But what makes him truly scary is his lack of moralities  he crosses every line that holds Batman to good. In doing so, he becomes Batman's opposite. And equal. Heath Ledger plays the Joker with an eccentric freedom hardly seen before, and in doing so comes as close as humanly possible to the demented Joker of the comic books. His stammering speech and shuffling walk exemplify the chaos in his mind. The Joker brings such dread, that you anticipate yet fear his arrival on screen  there are no limits to what he would do. In facing him, Batman and Harvey Dent are pushed to a limit that neither should cross.At 2hrs 32mins, the movie is relentless and unforgiving. "The night is darkest before the dawn", proclaims Harvey Dent in once scene. "Why so serious?" asks the Joker in another. Christopher Nolan humorlessly depicts Gotham at its darkest hour, and weaves a saga of crime that is not expected of a superhero movie. The characters are given a depth that makes them as believable as timeless. Indeed, the movie transcends the comic-book-movie genre to reach a level of sophistication hardly ever attributed to superheroes. It makes for almost-a-must multiple watch.In becoming what it is, where the movie does disappoint is in its superhero parts. In favor of the story, sacrifices are made of Batman. Being one of the world's favorite super heroes, it does become injustice to not depict his iconography  visual representations of his towering persona, the batcave being replaced with a secret garage, the Harvey Dent arc in favor of the Batman-Joker conflict. Christopher Nolan, in making an exemplary movie has sacrificed Batman and pushed himself into a corner. If he does complete his trilogy, he would have to go back to the dark knight.

ipc-title__text: A satisfactory improvement on Batman Begins.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I must say I went into this movie with low expectations as I was pretty disappointed with Batman Begins. As I do not really want to nit-pick or write a novel on the reasons why I didn't think much of Batman begins, I'll skip that and tell you what I liked about The Dark Knight: Quite simply, The JOKER! Best villain of the new millennium in my opinion! I don't want to give anything away for the people who haven't yet seen this film but let's just say the Joker is a true psychopathic killer. No boundaries, no remorse, just a cold blooded lunatic brilliantly portrayed by Heath Ledger in the best role I have ever seen him in. I now have a new found respect for Heath, he truly is a talented and gifted actor.Also really good in this film was Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent but once again I won't specify any details as I do not want to spoil anything. I must say I also preferred Maggie Gylanhall in the role of Rachel as poised to the average Katie Holmes.My major beef with this film sadly is Batman! Now don't get me wrong, I think Christian Bale is a really talented actor but unfortunately for me it doesn't work with his Batman persona. For one, the voice is stupid and he sounds like a wrestler when he speaks and I could barely make out what he was saying. Another annoying thing he would do was stick his lips out really strangely when he was in the Bat suit.....why????? This is really unfortunate because the whole point in seeing a Batman film is to see Batman!!! If you don't agree with the portrayal of the main character, it's very hard to fully enjoy and appreciate the film. I may be old school but I must say I prefer the Tim Burton versions! Not the Joel Schumacher ones though, they are stupid and childish. Another problem I have with this film is the "shakey-camera" style of filming for the action sequences throughout the film. This technique makes it very hard to see what's actually going on and when I watch a fight scene, I like to see exactly what's happening and I want to see every punch or kick connect instead of blurry-flashy images! It's a shame that this way of filming has become so popular in Hollywood in the last decade. Still, The Dark Knight is definitely worth seeing as it is still a great superhero blockbuster! But don't let all the media hype blow it out of preportion for you because in reality, it's not THAT great.

Great crime drama. Excellent story and acceptable plot. Ledger was brilliant, and this new characterization of the joker was fresh and thrilling and still true to the origins of the character.But seriously... Bale is flat and lifeless as Wayne, and ridiculously overdoes the gruff Batman voice, but that's nothing new to fans of Batman Begins. The real depressing fact here is the way the scenes just sort of meander around, with no real direct, strong editing to point the way. Eckhart and Oldman's scenes together resemble a quick read in a hotel the night before a shoot, and after their first three scenes the points have all been made and repeated and I just wish the movie would move forward. When it does, you're rewarded with a clever build into a stylish action sequence that doesn't stick to close to the rules of continuity, but doesn't stray too far from the path either, usually ending with an abrupt cut to yet another "plot development" scene with Eckhart and Oldman, and maybe Bale standing around to fill out the screen.Not a terrible movie, but not the masterpiece it's being hailed as. Too long and too loose. Another month on the script, another month shooting for better takes from the leading men, and another week in the editing room would have turned out something near perfect, but for now, it'll fill the void inside you that yearns for films based on comic books.

ipc-title__text: If the votes went up to 11, I'd give this movie a 100
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Somehow you knew seeing the trailers that this movie could possibly be one of the best ever but you tell yourself, "Nah, you're just buying the hype." Well it's better than it's hype and when nominating movies for best-movies-of-all-time lists you have to let it cool for a while, but I wouldn't be surprised if this went down in history as one of the big ones.We'd all heard that Heath was amazing in this and it's absolutely true. It wasn't like he was acting. It was like the Joker was leaking out of his pores. Because not only was he absolutely this character, but the character he created is in itself a masterpiece. Of course you have to also give credit to the Nolans who wrote the character. The way that this written character and this actor came together to create a whole other kind of being will have to be explained scientifically someday. And I'm sure I won't even understand the explanation because it's close to something I stopped believing in a long time ago, and that's magic. They caught lightning in a bottle if you will. You'll have to see it to believe it.But here's the problem with a performance like this, it can blow the other actors out of the water. But in an amazing feat by the entire cast, no one is left out to dry. Everyone is tip-top. And one of my favorite actors, Aaron Eckhart, does such wonderful work in this. It's almost sad that he won't get more attention for it because the focus is on Heath, but I'm sure eventually everyone will come around. Harvey Dent goes through so much. I can't explain further without spoiling, but Eckhart went through a full range of emotion in this film. There is a scene with him and Heath that is already one of my favorite scenes ever. Remember the restaurant scene in 'Heat'? Well, it's kid stuff compared to this one. That's right, I said it.Now let me say something about Christian Bale. I think he may possibly be the best actor of his generation. And in this film he allows everyone else to take the shine. Don't get me wrong. He does the work and does it well but some other actors might be threatened and you'd notice some histrionics to garner the spotlight, especially when they're the title character, but not Bale. His slow and steady Batman was like the rock holding everything in place. Like Alfred is to Bruce Wayne, Bale was to his other actors.Assembling such an outstanding cast, writing such an intricate film, and directing the whole thing is Christopher Nolan, who is now officially one of my favorite directors. I loved 'The Prestige'. On repeated viewings, it still knocks me on my butt. I was shocked at how high I had to include that film on my all time favorites list (yes I keep a list). Usually it takes me a while to bump something up out of respect to the other films but I thought it was brilliant and couldn't help myself. Well, I'm not even going to attempt to crack open my list for 'The Dark Knight' for a while. I fear for my top ten. The imagery, the music, costume design are all perfect. I mean there had to be something wrong with it right? I did have one complaint. But realizing that the plot point in question may not be what it seems, means I can't even complain about that. What I think happened may have not happened and even if it did then it's just a matter of preference and doesn't have anything to do with how insanely stupendous and awe-inspiringly magnificent 'The Dark Knight' is.Who shouldn't see this movie? People with no senses. Maybe that one guy or gal you hate, so they won't get to enjoy such a gift. It's been 5 days since the first time I saw it, 1 since the second and I haven't stopped talking about it. I can't stop saying words like "best" and "ever" and "amazing". I'm going to wish as hard as I can that the Academy will decide that they need an award for Best Cast this year before it's too late. It's early but I'm hoping this at least gets a Best Picture nomination. If you haven't seen it yet, I'd like to see a doctor's note.

ipc-title__text: It's a Great movie, but clearly has controlled the audience minds.
Good, but far from the #1 movie of all-time
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I don't normally comment on films on this site, but when I saw that this movie was rated by users as the #1 movie of all-time, I had to set the record straight.Yes, while this is a good movie with great cinematography and a great performance by the late Heath Ledger, it is far from being the #1 movie of all-time. It is not even the #1 movie of the summer (Iron Man, for one, was better). Nor is it the best movie in the series (Batman Begins is better). There are plot holes galore and the chemistry between Maggie Gyllenhall's character and Batman/Wayne and Dent is simply lacking.Those who rate this movie #1 all-time clearly have not seen Raging Bull, Clockwork Orange, Rear Window, Casablanca or any number of other all-time great films. This movie should not even be in the top 200 all-time.Good...but not the "masterpiece" other users suggest it is.

Good acting. Good start to the movie. Good special effects.Not very good use of plot devices. The second half of the movie is full of moments that will leave you scratching your head. If the movie didn't attempt to set a high standard at the start it wouldn't have been a problem. But they started with a standard then abandoned that standard...too bad...maybe it could have been top 100.This is definitely "wait until on DVD" material...although the special effects could be a compelling reason to see it in a good theater.It was sad to see a great actor in the midst of a great performance who is no longer with us.

I saw this movie at the midnight premiere, with a bunch of overexcited friends, and I was expecting to see another mediocre superhero movie, with a throwaway plot and some nice nostalgic moments to keep us interested. I was totally blown away by what I saw that night.The Dark Knight is a masterpiece compared to all other comic inspired movies. It makes Spiderman 3 look like Shumakers Batman and Robin(with the nipples). The plot is incredibly deep, with unexpected twists and turns all along the way. There are many moments where the viewer is completely caught off guard, as they are setup to expect something to happen, only to have the complete opposite take place instead. The film also makes use of multiple climaxes, which made for a great roller coaster ride of a film, but also made the length of the film a bit more apparent and made the plot feel like it was dragging on.Heath Ledger gives what is possibly the best performance as Joker since Mark Hamills in the animated series, thought the two are very different. Ledger gives a Joker that is both insane and indifferent, he isn't interested in money or power, but only wants to watch the world, and the batman, burn. The only bad part about Ledgers performance is that he won't be able to return. Although the Joker pretty much stole the show, the rest of the cast gives a solid performance. The only performance gripe I had was the masked man himself, who is given a raspy hiss of a voice by Bale, which I found to be very annoying. I thought Bales rendition of Bruce Wayne(no mask) was very good though.The special effects are also great though they are rarely used. I actually didn't realize that CGI animation was present in the film until I saw it the second time, it's employed very skillfully. The fight scenes are fairly good, better than your average batman fight scenes. Although most of the action scenes are pretty forgettable in the midst of all the great drama going on, there is a chase/car-fight scene involving the joker, a SWAT convoy of armored cars, the batmobile, a helicopter and a huge semi battling it out in the tunnels and streets of gotham that is truly exciting to watch.The Dark Knight stands out above the rest of the super hero genre because even if DK was in no way associated with the modern legend of Batman, if the hero in the film was just a generic caped crime fighter, it would still be a considered a great movie. While the association with legendary Batman certainly makes the movie more accessible, it doesn't lean on it's roots for support the way most other super hero movies do. A superb movie that is enjoyable to Batman lovers and non-batman(mythological creature?) lovers alike

ipc-title__text: it was good but not "THAT" good
Not really sure what to call it, but it's no masterpiece
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I went into The Dark Knight with great anticipation. Of all the superheroes, I love the character Batman (at least the one in the comics and the more famous cartoon series, even Batman Beyond). This movie starts very slow, so I waited and waited and waited for this great, awesome masterpiece...but it never came.The reason Batman is such a great character is that he like Two face has two sides. In this movie we never see them. He one sided, one dimensional overshadowed by every other character in the movie, especially Heath Ledger's joker and Gary Oldman's Jim Gordon. We see real emotion in these characters, we even see emotion in Micheal Caine and Morgan Freeman's characters but no emotion from our hero/antihero Batman. All we get is a long convoluted story to catch a madman and a horribly, over the top raspy voiced super human, thug. The writers don't ever take the time to dwell into the psychology of this man who night after night goes out to fight crime. Even when he confronted with copycats we see little emotion from Bruce Wayne, just dumb dialog.Now I thought Katie Holmes was bad in the Batman Begins but Ms. Gyllenhaal is worse and sorry to say this but I was glad when they killed her. She was pitiful looking and annoying. Aaron Eckhart is okay as Harvey Dent but I wish they had the guts to use a Black man like the original Dent.Lastly I want to say a few things about the so called message. Good writers can make a point without smashing you in the face with it. Obviously these weren't good writers. The film reverts to suspenseful music in the place of real suspense and give us two boats filled with plastic characters, when they should have spent that time not showing us what they were doing but what Bruce Wayne/Batman was thinking and feeling. But instead we got long-winded preachy speeches and an obviously wounded hero running off like nothing was hurt. By the look on most of the patrons faces in my theater, they were disappointed too. Too bad, Ledger's Joker steals the show and Batman is buried by him.

ipc-title__text: Pure Cinematic Brilliance / A High-Octane Thrill Ride
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Outside of the ArcLight's legendary Cinerama Dome movie theater complex in Hollywood, where Star Wars made its debut 31 years ago, Batman's motorcycle from The Dark Knight stood behind a rope for all to see and photograph, as a security guard kept a watchful eye. Inside of the theater, a Batman costume hung, flanked by the Joker's henchman's masks in transparent cases. The purple suit donned by Heath Ledger as the Joker, its color-matched gloves hanging from the arms stood eerily by, as a kind of headless specimen. Some were fortunate enough to get movie posters, from the nearby decked-out trailer.As I sat in the packed theater, an emcee gave us all a hearty welcome; the trademark bat shadow looming prominently above, on the curtains behind him. You could almost hear a pin drop as Gotham City illuminated the slightly curved screen, in a panoramic view reminiscent of the IMAX.There is no doubt that every person associated with The Dark Knight, brought their A game to the experience. It was obvious that the city of Chicago, a perfect surrogate Gotham City, was more than welcoming to the film crew  allowing shots and sequences that are rarely filmed in a large metropolitan city. It is hard to imagine some of those frames managing to be made, even in a movie town such as L.A.This is a film that deftly transcends a noirish atmosphere, blending in concert, with the big budget effects. The temperament of the film, of course, is almost exclusively due to the set designs and character studies by each and every actor. In many large-scale films, the heroes and villains are drawn precisely, however, every character in The Dark Knight is so multi-layered, that it made watching a film adapted from a comic book more plausible. The identity crisis, and the resultant delusion and desolation that each character experiences, is a startling contrast to the traditional hero-warrior genre.The presence of Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman, provide the perfect backdrop for Christian Bale's vigilante, Darth Vader-esquire Batman, the genius of Heath Ledger's psychopathic, punked-out Joker, and Maggie Gyllenhall's perfectly believable, emotionally tormented Rachel Dawes - all the way to Aaron Eckhart's remarkably transformational portrayal of Harvey Two-Face. Many of the actors in this film were schooled and rooted in the character-driven independent film world, and it shows. If ever there was a dream cast, this is it.Every member of the cast who has been interviewed, has expressed the highest respect and admiration for Heath Ledger's brilliant characterization of the relentlessly psychotic, maniacally sadistic Joker. It is therefore no surprise, that it is virtually impossible to take your eyes off of him when he is on screen.Even more disturbing than the Joker's shades of A Clockwork Orange, with the anarchistic tendencies of the Sex Pistols punk band, is the ever-present undercurrent of masochism that propels him. I choose chaos, he proclaims, and chaos is exactly what occurs, every time he is encountered. On a psychological level - choosing chaos is something that few would admit to; it shows the disturbingly masochistic nature that permeates the soul of the worst kind of terrorist  with nothing left to lose. There is nothing more chillingly dangerous than self-hatred. Heath Ledger's Joker will go down in history as one of the most amazing villains ever portrayed on screen.The Joker enjoys toying with his prey; his survival, in a way, depends upon Batman's. He knows that humanity is what is lost, in the pursuit of money, fame and power. The greatest psychosis of the Joker, is that he has no fear of dying  or exposing his identity. It's not about money. It's about sending a message, he hisses. You can't negotiate with a masochistic, psychopathic terrorist.As if the entire spectacle isn't enough, there are fun-house Halloween types of surprises that can jolt you right out of your seat. This is the kind of film that everyone can appreciate, whether they identify with comic book stories or not. The plot and characters are drawn so well, that the makeup and props never get in the way of what makes a film spectacular: great storytelling.All of the characters struggle with their own demons, in one of the most enduringly artful ensemble casts ever to be seen in a high-octane thrill ride film experience. In a time when it is never certain if a film can live up to its hype, The Dark Knight definitely delivers, and then some. One thing is for sure: the genius of this film will never be forgotten.

ipc-title__text: Incredibly Mindblowing. The Best Film of 2008!
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Dark Knight was really worth the wait! I waited...let's see...14 months. Wow, thats a long time. Ever since Batman Begins, and the way it ended with the joker card and Batman saying "I'll look into it." I was like "They have to make a sequel!". And nothing for 2 year...until May 2007, my prayers were answered. My friend told me of something about a new Batman movie in May, I researched, and found the website: (Whysoserious.com). Yes I may sound like a nerd, but I did go on the scavenger hunts looking for the teaser trailers and the posters and photos of the Joker. Then in 2008 with only 7 months to go, hearing all about the production, and Heath Ledger being the Joker, getting so hyped. On January 22, while watching the news, bad news darkens my day. Heath Ledger (April 4, 1979 - January 22, 2008) died of accidental overdose, I did not live for that day, a fantastic actor whose life was cut short sadly.After all the sadness, July 18 finally came along. I saw the The Dark Knight at Cinemark at 7:45 pm Opening night (I was not lucky enough to get my tickets for Thursday 12:00. The Dark Knight has to be the most incredible film I have seen this year. I surpasses Batman Begins in every aspect! (Batman Begins is a great film, The Dark Knight is just wayy better) Every little thing about it was fantastic!! The editing, the direction, the cinematography, the score, the effects, the acting. The acting, Heath Ledger put on the best performance I have ever seen put on film. Aaron Eckhart was just as great as Heath was! Christian Bale, Morgan Freeman, Michael Caine, Maggie Gynllenhaal (who was a great replacement) all did fantasitc. I really have to give the standing ovation to Heath Leger, he did the absolute best in this film. Rest in peace Heath, you are missed. Two warnings about seeing this, It is really long 152 mins (2 1/2 hrs) so don't quibble, noting seems to slow down at all. The other warning is that, parents don't take your children that are younger than 12 years old. The Joker is quite scary, and the way he kills people is very disturbing, how he got the cuts is explained. The Dark Knight really is the best film of 2008! (Wall-E is equally good, but go see this) You won't wanna miss this one in the theater (or even IMAX) because if you do, you'll be missing out on one of the greats. 10/10

well you all knew this was coming so here goes my review of The Dark Knight.this movie is phenomenal!! you all probably figured that is what i would say but let me explain my reasoning besides the fact that its Batman. well to start it off, Batman Begins is one of my favorite movies and The Dark Knight expands on everything that was great about the first one. the acting is one of the main draws here, with Christopher Nolan expertly showcasing the scenes of dialogue between characters. Nolan manages to highlight just plain old talking into something amazing. the entire cast is superb (with Maggie Gyllenhall replacing the atrocious Katie Holmes) but the best addition is, of course, Heath Ledger. now during the course of this epic 2 and a half hour masterpiece Ledger's Joker is one of the greatest performances you will ever lay your eyes on. the things he does with this character are just mind-boggling. it blows Jack Nicholson's portrayal out of the water. he is the absolute best part of this movie. but it is just heart breaking to know once the lights come up in the theater that this is the last time you will ever see a new complete performance from the great Heath Ledger. his performance most certainly deserves a posthumous Oscar nomination for best supporting actor.another great addition is Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent/Two Face. yes in this movie he does show up as Two Face and he is awesome! also the twists and turns in this movie will just shock you. its an expertly crafted script and cast and is so beautifully directed. and even as long as it is, the movie just zips by. it is the shortest feeling 2 and half hours i have ever experienced at the movies and i wanted more. but of course it is set up for a 3rd that it should be required to make. so as it stands The Dark Knight is my pick for the best film for 2008 and i award it the score of 10 out of 10.

ipc-title__text: Not just the best comic book based movie, but best movie of the year
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I saw the movie a couple of hours ago and I am blown away. It was spectacular, I'm seeing it again in a couple of days. This movie surpassed every other comic book based film-including the first Batman-in overall depth, character development, plot complexity, and yes, acting. Nolan did the near impossible, he took a man running around fighting bad guys in a bat suit-one who's face looks like a clown-and created a modern crime drama-a realistic interpretation of an unrealistic concept. It was gritty and simply delicious.This movie surpasses the original batman not because of it's modern day action, or special effects, but because of it's sound story and-of course-of ledger's brilliant acting. There are several plot developments and twists that had me bouncing out of my seat. Burton's Batman was very good, it set the bar, and that bar has remained unsurpassed until TDK. Burton's Batman was set in a comic like world, it felt detached from Our concept of reality-but of course, this is what Burton intends to do. It's his mind literally bleeding on film. This is what makes his movies so entertaining, his ability to bring his own private images to on screen in stunning clarity; his originality is stupendous. I say all this because I want ya'll to know How much I love Burton, but that doesn't change the fact that this movie is much better than it. This movie felt like it could actually happen today. The terroristic theme of the film was great.Now, on to Ledger. His performance was better than Jacks in every way possible. ipc-title__text: Better than Batman Begins? I'd say it's a draw.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Dark Knight (2008) was a really good movie, this should be obvious by now. I don't want to go through everything I liked about this movie because that would just take way too long. However, that doesn't mean there weren't any flaws in the flick.One thing I will point out, however, is that I absolutely loved how they handled multiple villains. Most super hero movie sequels tend to inject loads of villains in an effort to up the ante, but they all completely suck at it. Here, they juggled it perfectly: Scarecrow made a brief appearance at the beginning, but was quickly caught. The Joker was the main villain, and dealt with for the bulk of the movie. And Two-Face was really just thrown at the end to add a bit more tension.Now for the flaws: 1. Maggie Gyllenhaal confused me. It took me a little while to figure out that she was the replacement for Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes. I also thought she was kind of ugly and not a very good actor. 2. Christian Bale was mostly good, but his deep Batman voice was even cheesier than it was in Batman Begins. It almost sounded like he couldn't breathe through his nose. 3. They didn't really wrap up The Joker's story. The last we saw of him, he was just hanging from a roof, and he seemed like a smart enough (and violent enough) guy to get out of that situation - though, with Heath Ledger now deceased I doubt we'd see a reprisal of The Joker in this series. 4. I thought the whole sonar phone thing was a little dumb - sorry. The whole "no man should have this power" speech just seemed politically pointed and crammed in where it didn't really fit.Keep in mind, these are only minor nitpicks. It was a good movie. Did I like it better than Batman Begins? Eh, I don't know. The back story in Begins was really awesome, but the villains in Dark Knight were really amazing - I'd say it's a draw.

ipc-html-content-inner-div: I must say I went into this movie with low expectations as I was pretty disappointed with Batman Begins. As I do not really want to nit-pick or write a novel on the reasons why I didn't think much of Batman begins, I'll skip that and tell you what I liked about The Dark Knight: Quite simply, The JOKER! Best villain of the new millennium in my opinion! I don't want to give anything away for the people who haven't yet seen this film but let's just say the Joker is a true psychopathic killer. No boundaries, no remorse, just a cold blooded lunatic brilliantly portrayed by Heath Ledger in the best role I have ever seen him in. I now have a new found respect for Heath, he truly is a talented and gifted actor.Also really good in this film was Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent but once again I won't specify any details as I do not want to spoil anything. I must say I also preferred Maggie Gylanhall in the role of Rachel as poised to the average Katie Holmes.My major beef with this film sadly is Batman! Now don't get me wrong, I think Christian Bale is a really talented actor but unfortunately for me it doesn't work with his Batman persona. For one, the voice is stupid and he sounds like a wrestler when he speaks and I could barely make out what he was saying. Another annoying thing he would do was stick his lips out really strangely when he was in the Bat suit.....why????? This is really unfortunate because the whole point in seeing a Batman film is to see Batman!!! If you don't agree with the portrayal of the main character, it's very hard to fully enjoy and appreciate the film. I may be old school but I must say I prefer the Tim Burton versions! Not the Joel Schumacher ones though, they are stupid and childish. Another problem I have with this film is the "shakey-camera" style of filming for the action sequences throughout the film. This technique makes it very hard to see what's actually going on and when I watch a fight scene, I like to see exactly what's happening and I want to see every punch or kick connect instead of blurry-flashy images! It's a shame that this way of filming has become so popular in Hollywood in the last decade. Still, The Dark Knight is definitely worth seeing as it is still a great superhero blockbuster! But don't let all the media hype blow it out of preportion for you because in reality, it's not THAT great.

Great crime drama. Excellent story and acceptable plot. Ledger was brilliant, and this new characterization of the joker was fresh and thrilling and still true to the origins of the character.But seriously... Bale is flat and lifeless as Wayne, and ridiculously overdoes the gruff Batman voice, but that's nothing new to fans of Batman Begins. The real depressing fact here is the way the scenes just sort of meander around, with no real direct, strong editing to point the way. Eckhart and Oldman's scenes together resemble a quick read in a hotel the night before a shoot, and after their first three scenes the points have all been made and repeated and I just wish the movie would move forward. When it does, you're rewarded with a clever build into a stylish action sequence that doesn't stick to close to the rules of continuity, but doesn't stray too far from the path either, usually ending with an abrupt cut to yet another "plot development" scene with Eckhart and Oldman, and maybe Bale standing around to fill out the screen.Not a terrible movie, but not the masterpiece it's being hailed as. Too long and too loose. Another month on the script, another month shooting for better takes from the leading men, and another week in the editing room would have turned out something near perfect, but for now, it'll fill the void inside you that yearns for films based on comic books.

ipc-title__text: If the votes went up to 11, I'd give this movie a 100
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Somehow you knew seeing the trailers that this movie could possibly be one of the best ever but you tell yourself, "Nah, you're just buying the hype." Well it's better than it's hype and when nominating movies for best-movies-of-all-time lists you have to let it cool for a while, but I wouldn't be surprised if this went down in history as one of the big ones.We'd all heard that Heath was amazing in this and it's absolutely true. It wasn't like he was acting. It was like the Joker was leaking out of his pores. Because not only was he absolutely this character, but the character he created is in itself a masterpiece. Of course you have to also give credit to the Nolans who wrote the character. The way that this written character and this actor came together to create a whole other kind of being will have to be explained scientifically someday. And I'm sure I won't even understand the explanation because it's close to something I stopped believing in a long time ago, and that's magic. They caught lightning in a bottle if you will. You'll have to see it to believe it.But here's the problem with a performance like this, it can blow the other actors out of the water. But in an amazing feat by the entire cast, no one is left out to dry. Everyone is tip-top. And one of my favorite actors, Aaron Eckhart, does such wonderful work in this. It's almost sad that he won't get more attention for it because the focus is on Heath, but I'm sure eventually everyone will come around. Harvey Dent goes through so much. I can't explain further without spoiling, but Eckhart went through a full range of emotion in this film. There is a scene with him and Heath that is already one of my favorite scenes ever. Remember the restaurant scene in 'Heat'? Well, it's kid stuff compared to this one. That's right, I said it.Now let me say something about Christian Bale. I think he may possibly be the best actor of his generation. And in this film he allows everyone else to take the shine. Don't get me wrong. He does the work and does it well but some other actors might be threatened and you'd notice some histrionics to garner the spotlight, especially when they're the title character, but not Bale. His slow and steady Batman was like the rock holding everything in place. Like Alfred is to Bruce Wayne, Bale was to his other actors.Assembling such an outstanding cast, writing such an intricate film, and directing the whole thing is Christopher Nolan, who is now officially one of my favorite directors. I loved 'The Prestige'. On repeated viewings, it still knocks me on my butt. I was shocked at how high I had to include that film on my all time favorites list (yes I keep a list). Usually it takes me a while to bump something up out of respect to the other films but I thought it was brilliant and couldn't help myself. Well, I'm not even going to attempt to crack open my list for 'The Dark Knight' for a while. I fear for my top ten. The imagery, the music, costume design are all perfect. I mean there had to be something wrong with it right? I did have one complaint. But realizing that the plot point in question may not be what it seems, means I can't even complain about that. What I think happened may have not happened and even if it did then it's just a matter of preference and doesn't have anything to do with how insanely stupendous and awe-inspiringly magnificent 'The Dark Knight' is.Who shouldn't see this movie? People with no senses. Maybe that one guy or gal you hate, so they won't get to enjoy such a gift. It's been 5 days since the first time I saw it, 1 since the second and I haven't stopped talking about it. I can't stop saying words like "best" and "ever" and "amazing". I'm going to wish as hard as I can that the Academy will decide that they need an award for Best Cast this year before it's too late. It's early but I'm hoping this at least gets a Best Picture nomination. If you haven't seen it yet, I'd like to see a doctor's note.

I saw this movie at the midnight premiere, with a bunch of overexcited friends, and I was expecting to see another mediocre superhero movie, with a throwaway plot and some nice nostalgic moments to keep us interested. I was totally blown away by what I saw that night.The Dark Knight is a masterpiece compared to all other comic inspired movies. It makes Spiderman 3 look like Shumakers Batman and Robin(with the nipples). The plot is incredibly deep, with unexpected twists and turns all along the way. There are many moments where the viewer is completely caught off guard, as they are setup to expect something to happen, only to have the complete opposite take place instead. The film also makes use of multiple climaxes, which made for a great roller coaster ride of a film, but also made the length of the film a bit more apparent and made the plot feel like it was dragging on.Heath Ledger gives what is possibly the best performance as Joker since Mark Hamills in the animated series, thought the two are very different. Ledger gives a Joker that is both insane and indifferent, he isn't interested in money or power, but only wants to watch the world, and the batman, burn. The only bad part about Ledgers performance is that he won't be able to return. Although the Joker pretty much stole the show, the rest of the cast gives a solid performance. The only performance gripe I had was the masked man himself, who is given a raspy hiss of a voice by Bale, which I found to be very annoying. I thought Bales rendition of Bruce Wayne(no mask) was very good though.The special effects are also great though they are rarely used. I actually didn't realize that CGI animation was present in the film until I saw it the second time, it's employed very skillfully. The fight scenes are fairly good, better than your average batman fight scenes. Although most of the action scenes are pretty forgettable in the midst of all the great drama going on, there is a chase/car-fight scene involving the joker, a SWAT convoy of armored cars, the batmobile, a helicopter and a huge semi battling it out in the tunnels and streets of gotham that is truly exciting to watch.The Dark Knight stands out above the rest of the super hero genre because even if DK was in no way associated with the modern legend of Batman, if the hero in the film was just a generic caped crime fighter, it would still be a considered a great movie. While the association with legendary Batman certainly makes the movie more accessible, it doesn't lean on it's roots for support the way most other super hero movies do. A superb movie that is enjoyable to Batman lovers and non-batman(mythological creature?) lovers alike

This movie starts very slow, so I waited and waited and waited for this great, awesome masterpiece...but it never came.The reason Batman is such a great character is that he like Two face has two sides. Aaron Eckhart is okay as Harvey Dent but I wish they had the guts to use a Black man like the original Dent.Lastly I want to say a few things about the so called message. Good writers can make a point without smashing you in the face with it. Obviously these weren't good writers. The film reverts to suspenseful music in the place of real suspense and give us two boats filled with plastic characters, when they should have spent that time not showing us what they were doing but what Bruce Wayne/Batman was thinking and feeling. ipc-title__text: Pure Cinematic Brilliance / A High-Octane Thrill Ride
ipc-html-content-inner-div: Outside of the ArcLight's legendary Cinerama Dome movie theater complex in Hollywood, where Star Wars made its debut 31 years ago, Batman's motorcycle from The Dark Knight stood behind a rope for all to see and photograph, as a security guard kept a watchful eye. Inside of the theater, a Batman costume hung, flanked by the Joker's henchman's masks in transparent cases. The purple suit donned by Heath Ledger as the Joker, its color-matched gloves hanging from the arms stood eerily by, as a kind of headless specimen. Some were fortunate enough to get movie posters, from the nearby decked-out trailer.As I sat in the packed theater, an emcee gave us all a hearty welcome; the trademark bat shadow looming prominently above, on the curtains behind him. You could almost hear a pin drop as Gotham City illuminated the slightly curved screen, in a panoramic view reminiscent of the IMAX.There is no doubt that every person associated with The Dark Knight, brought their A game to the experience. It was obvious that the city of Chicago, a perfect surrogate Gotham City, was more than welcoming to the film crew  allowing shots and sequences that are rarely filmed in a large metropolitan city. It is hard to imagine some of those frames managing to be made, even in a movie town such as L.A.This is a film that deftly transcends a noirish atmosphere, blending in concert, with the big budget effects. The temperament of the film, of course, is almost exclusively due to the set designs and character studies by each and every actor. In many large-scale films, the heroes and villains are drawn precisely, however, every character in The Dark Knight is so multi-layered, that it made watching a film adapted from a comic book more plausible. The identity crisis, and the resultant delusion and desolation that each character experiences, is a startling contrast to the traditional hero-warrior genre.The presence of Michael Caine, Morgan Freeman and Gary Oldman, provide the perfect backdrop for Christian Bale's vigilante, Darth Vader-esquire Batman, the genius of Heath Ledger's psychopathic, punked-out Joker, and Maggie Gyllenhall's perfectly believable, emotionally tormented Rachel Dawes - all the way to Aaron Eckhart's remarkably transformational portrayal of Harvey Two-Face. Many of the actors in this film were schooled and rooted in the character-driven independent film world, and it shows. If ever there was a dream cast, this is it.Every member of the cast who has been interviewed, has expressed the highest respect and admiration for Heath Ledger's brilliant characterization of the relentlessly psychotic, maniacally sadistic Joker. It is therefore no surprise, that it is virtually impossible to take your eyes off of him when he is on screen.Even more disturbing than the Joker's shades of A Clockwork Orange, with the anarchistic tendencies of the Sex Pistols punk band, is the ever-present undercurrent of masochism that propels him. I choose chaos, he proclaims, and chaos is exactly what occurs, every time he is encountered. On a psychological level - choosing chaos is something that few would admit to; it shows the disturbingly masochistic nature that permeates the soul of the worst kind of terrorist  with nothing left to lose. There is nothing more chillingly dangerous than self-hatred. Heath Ledger's Joker will go down in history as one of the most amazing villains ever portrayed on screen.The Joker enjoys toying with his prey; his survival, in a way, depends upon Batman's. He knows that humanity is what is lost, in the pursuit of money, fame and power. The greatest psychosis of the Joker, is that he has no fear of dying  or exposing his identity. It's not about money. It's about sending a message, he hisses. You can't negotiate with a masochistic, psychopathic terrorist.As if the entire spectacle isn't enough, there are fun-house Halloween types of surprises that can jolt you right out of your seat. This is the kind of film that everyone can appreciate, whether they identify with comic book stories or not. The plot and characters are drawn so well, that the makeup and props never get in the way of what makes a film spectacular: great storytelling.All of the characters struggle with their own demons, in one of the most enduringly artful ensemble casts ever to be seen in a high-octane thrill ride film experience. In a time when it is never certain if a film can live up to its hype, The Dark Knight definitely delivers, and then some. One thing is for sure: the genius of this film will never be forgotten.

well you all knew this was coming so here goes my review of The Dark Knight.this movie is phenomenal!! you all probably figured that is what i would say but let me explain my reasoning besides the fact that its Batman. well to start it off, Batman Begins is one of my favorite movies and The Dark Knight expands on everything that was great about the first one. the acting is one of the main draws here, with Christopher Nolan expertly showcasing the scenes of dialogue between characters. Nolan manages to highlight just plain old talking into something amazing. the entire cast is superb (with Maggie Gyllenhall replacing the atrocious Katie Holmes) but the best addition is, of course, Heath Ledger. now during the course of this epic 2 and a half hour masterpiece Ledger's Joker is one of the greatest performances you will ever lay your eyes on. the things he does with this character are just mind-boggling. it blows Jack Nicholson's portrayal out of the water. he is the absolute best part of this movie. but it is just heart breaking to know once the lights come up in the theater that this is the last time you will ever see a new complete performance from the great Heath Ledger. his performance most certainly deserves a posthumous Oscar nomination for best supporting actor.another great addition is Aaron Eckhart as Harvey Dent/Two Face. yes in this movie he does show up as Two Face and he is awesome! also the twists and turns in this movie will just shock you. its an expertly crafted script and cast and is so beautifully directed. and even as long as it is, the movie just zips by. it is the shortest feeling 2 and half hours i have ever experienced at the movies and i wanted more. but of course it is set up for a 3rd that it should be required to make. so as it stands The Dark Knight is my pick for the best film for 2008 and i award it the score of 10 out of 10.

ipc-title__text: Not just the best comic book based movie, but best movie of the year
ipc-html-content-inner-div: I saw the movie a couple of hours ago and I am blown away. It was spectacular, I'm seeing it again in a couple of days. This movie surpassed every other comic book based film-including the first Batman-in overall depth, character development, plot complexity, and yes, acting. Nolan did the near impossible, he took a man running around fighting bad guys in a bat suit-one who's face looks like a clown-and created a modern crime drama-a realistic interpretation of an unrealistic concept. It was gritty and simply delicious.This movie surpasses the original batman not because of it's modern day action, or special effects, but because of it's sound story and-of course-of ledger's brilliant acting. There are several plot developments and twists that had me bouncing out of my seat. Burton's Batman was very good, it set the bar, and that bar has remained unsurpassed until TDK. Burton's Batman was set in a comic like world, it felt detached from Our concept of reality-but of course, this is what Burton intends to do. It's his mind literally bleeding on film. This is what makes his movies so entertaining, his ability to bring his own private images to on screen in stunning clarity; his originality is stupendous. I say all this because I want ya'll to know How much I love Burton, but that doesn't change the fact that this movie is much better than it. This movie felt like it could actually happen today. The terroristic theme of the film was great.Now, on to Ledger. His performance was better than Jacks in every way possible. The little facial reactions; the smacking of lips; the hand movements; the walk; acting at it's best. Jack's Joker was funny, Heath's was terrifying, he never gave an inch. At all times he was completely insane. It's a shame he passed, what a great performance his was. Maggie was excellent as Racheal, the depth of her character was bright at all times. Bale was superb, he is truly Batman. Morgan's performance was also fantastic, as well was Cain's. I gave this movie a 9/10 only because it had minor flaws; these flaws may even be nick picking, but in my head they exist. I didn't care that much for Two Face's distorted area of his face. I don't really know why, but It didn't have that stamp of authenticity to it, but this didn't detract from the greatness of the movie. Also, Bale's voice as batman sounded a bit overdone-almost like a grunt. I didn't care for this either. Other than that this movie lived up to the hype and in ways surpassed it.Enjoy the film!!

ipc-title__text: Better than Batman Begins? I'd say it's a draw.
ipc-html-content-inner-div: The Dark Knight (2008) was a really good movie, this should be obvious by now. I don't want to go through everything I liked about this movie because that would just take way too long. However, that doesn't mean there weren't any flaws in the flick.One thing I will point out, however, is that I absolutely loved how they handled multiple villains. Most super hero movie sequels tend to inject loads of villains in an effort to up the ante, but they all completely suck at it. Here, they juggled it perfectly: Scarecrow made a brief appearance at the beginning, but was quickly caught. The Joker was the main villain, and dealt with for the bulk of the movie. And Two-Face was really just thrown at the end to add a bit more tension.Now for the flaws: 1. Maggie Gyllenhaal confused me. It took me a little while to figure out that she was the replacement for Katie Holmes as Rachel Dawes. I also thought she was kind of ugly and not a very good actor. 2. Christian Bale was mostly good, but his deep Batman voice was even cheesier than it was in Batman Begins. It almost sounded like he couldn't breathe through his nose. 3. They didn't really wrap up The Joker's story. The last we saw of him, he was just hanging from a roof, and he seemed like a smart enough (and violent enough) guy to get out of that situation - though, with Heath Ledger now deceased I doubt we'd see a reprisal of The Joker in this series. 4. I thought the whole sonar phone thing was a little dumb - sorry. The whole "no man should have this power" speech just seemed politically pointed and crammed in where it didn't really fit.Keep in mind, these are only minor nitpicks. It was a good movie. Did I like it better than Batman Begins? Eh, I don't know. The back story in Begins was really awesome, but the villains in Dark Knight were really amazing - I'd say it's a draw.
